purpose: Reference library of real Google Earth Studio camera authoring used to inform VIDTOOLZ planner defaults. Operator directives (Mikko, 2026-08-08): (1) the Google Earth Studio template moves define good camera motion; (2) locally-present or VIDTOOLZ-generated .esp files do NOT qualify as motion-quality examples — qualifying references must come from the internet. Only APPROVED references influence production defaults.
evidence_hierarchy: original .esp > .esp + render > exported project data > video > description

references.shot: 10 s 4K Mount Kinabalu flyover — 23.3 km route, 6222→5044 m
references.approval_basis: operator directive (internet-sourced) + deliberate multi-property authoring: every keyframe eased, all five camera properties keyed on a shared grid, explicit final hold
what_it_teaches: every keyframe side is eased: easeIn arrivals, easeOut departures, auto elsewhere
transition handle spans ≈ 25–31% of the gap to the neighbor keyframe (x 0.125 on 0.4 spacing; x 0.1 on 0.4)
ALL motion (position, altitude, pan, tilt) completes at t=0.80 — the final 20% of the shot is a hold
properties are keyed together on a shared time grid (0 / 0.4 / 0.8)

references.classification: EXTERNAL / HUMAN-AUTHORED (internet — b-roll for a published video essay)
references.shot: 16.7 s 60 fps space-to-region blast: 65,117 km → 179 km in the first 10%, then a 90% hold
what_it_teaches: motion can be extremely front-loaded: the entire move fits the first ~10%, the rest is a framing hold
mid-move keyframe uses ES auto easing with influence 0.35 and true y-handle components
holds are authored by simply ending keyframes early — value persists

references.shot: 5 s space pullback, 828 km ground path
references.approval_basis: operator directive (internet-sourced); corroborates easing shapes on a minimal 2-keyframe move
what_it_teaches: departure: auto ease, handle x = 0.2 of the segment
arrival: custom ease-in, handle x = −0.32 of the segment, influence 0.4

references.classification: EXTERNAL / HUMAN-AUTHORED via the Google Zoom-To Quick Start template (internet)
references.shot: 25 s descent 20,747→747 m completing at t=0.20, then POI-locked drift (21.8 km route)
references.approval_basis: operator directives (internet-sourced + templates define good moves): its transitions are BYTE-SIMILAR to the disqualified local ekayle1 — two independent authors converge exactly on easeOut x0.05 departure / custom x-0.198 infl 0.99 arrival / auto ±0.066 / 0.2 grid / POI lock, identifying these as the Google Zoom-To template’s own authored values
what_it_teaches: the Google Zoom-To template shape: 6 keyframes on a 0.2 grid, descent completes at t=0.20, drift for the remainder
template arrival = custom ease-in spanning ~0.99 of the gap, influence 0.99 (a full-segment deceleration)
template interiors = auto ±0.33 of gap, influence 0.5; departure easeOut 0.25 of gap
POI target lock instead of rotation keyframes
